Subject: ACME - RAG eval: post-call recap + recommended next steps

Jordan / Elena — great to meet you both this morning. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the RAG evaluation:

Summary:
- Goal: Improve accuracy and grounding for internal knowledge Q&A (policy and product docs) while keeping median latency under 650ms for 512-token responses.
- Current baseline: bi-encoder retriever + lightweight bi-encoder reranker, embedding model: text-embedding-3-small, recall@5 ~ 0.68, hallucination rate ~ 12% on the seed prompt set.

Redwood recommendations (high level):
1) Retriever: dense-embedding retriever (text-embedding-3-medium) with per-document chunking at ~ 400 tokens and 384-d overlap. Top-k initial retrieval = 50, then re-rank top 10.
2) Reranker: cross-encoder reranker (cross-encoder-small) for final ranking — improves MRR and grounding but adds ~80-120ms. Alternative: hybrid two-stage (bi-encoder recall + lightweight cross re-rank) to balance cost/latency.
3) Model for generation: Redwood-13B-quant for final outputs (good tradeoff of cost and factuality); Redwood-7B as a canary for latency-sensitive flows.
4) Prompting & grounding: use structured system prompt with explicit "source:" blocks and returned citations. We'll share a prompt set (attached) and a suggested schema for citation formatting.

Evaluation plan and metrics we propose to run next:
- Primary metrics: MRR@10, Recall@5, Grounding Score (percent of answers with at least 1 correct citation), Hallucination Rate (manual sample), median latency (p50) and p95 latency.
- Dataset: 1.2k seed questions you provided + 800 synthetic edge cases (confusing entity names, partial docs).
- A/B: baseline (current bi-encoder only) vs. proposed (dense retriever + cross-encoder reranker + Redwood-13B-quant) with 25%/75% traffic split for 48h.

Attachments: acme_rag_eval_results_v2.pdf (initial benchmark), prompt_sets.zip (seed prompts & edge-case prompts). Links: benchmarks drive folder + HubSpot deal link below.

Next steps / ask:
- Rishi and Dev will propose exact retrieval hyperparams and a reranker candidate matrix by EOD today.
- Can you confirm availability for a 45m technical tuning session next week (Mon/Tue preferred)?
- Final ask: please confirm primary success metric (MRR vs. Grounding) — we recommend prioritizing Grounding for compliance-sensitive answers.

Thanks,
Marissa

Jordan — good questions. Quick answers and concrete numbers from our recent internal tests (same evaluation harness used for your seed set):

Latency impact (approx):
- Baseline (bi-encoder retriever, no rerank, Redwood-7B): p50 210ms, p95 540ms (including generation for 512 tokens).
- Two-stage (dense retriever top-50, bi-encoder re-rank top-50, lightweight cross re-rank top-10, Redwood-13B-quant generation): p50 ~ 470ms, p95 ~ 860ms.
- Full cross-encoder on top-50 (no lightweight stage): p50 ~ 560ms, p95 ~ 1.05s.

Notes: numbers include network overhead typical for our hosted flow. If you pin to Dedicated with colocated rerank workers we can shave ~120ms off p95.

Grounding definition: we compute Grounding Score as: percent of model answers that include at least one citation whose source text contains the ground-truth answer span. For A/B we recommend a manual sample (n=200) with adjudication to measure hallucination rate and precision of citation.

Reranker recommendation matrix (short):
- cross-encoder-small (best grounding, higher latency/cost) — recommended for initial eval and narrow QA flows (support articles).
- cross-encoder-medium (better accuracy, higher cost) — if you need very high precision and can tolerate latency.
- bi-encoder + lightweight re-rank (fast, cheaper) — recommended for high-volume FAQ pages where recall matters more than precise grounding.

Retriever hyperparams (proposed initial):
- embedding model: text-embedding-3-medium
- chunk size: 400 tokens, 384 overlap
- top_k_retrieval: 50 (increase if recall < 0.72)
- final_rerank_top_k: 10

A/B + regression protection:
- Run A/B for 48 hours or 1000 unique queries whichever comes first.
- Track a quality regression dashboard: daily MRR delta, Grounding Score delta, Hallucination Rate. We will set an automatic rollback threshold of >3pt drop in Grounding Score or >5pt increase in Hallucination.

Sample citation format (we'll attach a doc with examples). Example response snippet:
"Answer: Our policy requires two signatures for changes to production.
Sources:
  - doc://acme/policies/change-control#section-4 (paragraph 2)
  - doc://acme/engineering/release-process#qa (line 10)"

I'll upload a short example run and the re-ranker candidate performance table to the Drive link now. Dev will follow up with an infra note about Dedicated vs Hosted latency trade-offs.

Rishi
